items.caption:
Amazon CEO Andy Jassy says AI will mean fewer humans doing what they do today.

He doesn't say no people. He expects new jobs, some we can't predict yet, and much smaller teams of people who work across functions, because the model gets them 80% of the way there.

Would you rather work on a team of 5 or a team of 50?

Source: a16z, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy on Reinventing Amazon for the AI Era. Full video: youtube.com/watch?v=-YMMRQ1qscI

items.caption:
Andy Jassy's AI advice to young people, and to his own kids: you can't run away from it.

He says to use it a lot and try things outside your comfort zone. Neither of his kids were developers, and they have used AI to build applications. He also says it doesn't replace critical reasoning and thinking.

What's the first thing you built with AI?

items.caption:
Andy Jassy predicts companies will have to rewrite almost all of their code to work with agents.

He says most startups today begin agent native. Larger companies have to learn to build at that pace, and in his opinion the ones that move slowly will be more vulnerable to startups.

Who has the advantage here: the startup or the incumbent with the customers?

items.caption:
Jensen Huang says writing code at a computer is going to get automated away.

He compares it to long division, which his generation had to learn. But he says the hard problems, like physics, chemistry, biology, computer science and systems thinking, especially where those fields intersect, will never go away.

If you were 18 today, what would you study?

Source: Y Combinator, Jensen Huang: The Mindset That Built NVIDIA. Full video: youtube.com/watch?v=I4B37S1dyQQ

items.caption:
Jensen Huang says he vividly remembers how scared he was to raise money for NVIDIA.

He bought a 500-page book on how to start a company and figured he'd be out of business before he finished it. He felt he couldn't answer investors' questions, and says he barely can even today. His lesson: none of that stuff matters, and you'll always have things you don't know.

What almost stopped you from starting?
